summary: The production correction is already present in the prepared main checkout: NPU unquantized MoE post-processing preserves canonical w13/w2 parameter layouts and transposes only at execution, so subsequent separate gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj disk loads remain valid. Added focused regression coverage for post-process followed by reload, the minimum intermediate-size boundary, and independent replacement of both w13 halves.

tests.what_was_measured: Three CPU tests exercised the NPU post-processing branch with format casting mocked, then loaded separate gate, up, and down tensors through the actual FusedMoE loader. Cases covered intermediate sizes 1 and 3 and verified that both fused halves overwrite prior values independently.

On one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), loaded separate 1408x64 BF16 gate and up tensors into a 2816x64 fused destination and independently compared both halves; gate checksum 4060041216.0 and up checksum 4060057088.0.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-41e2ae4a818a/venv/bin/python -c '<pre-fix transposed NPU layout followed by FusedMoE._load_w13>'
tests.what_was_measured: Recreated the obsolete NPU post-processing layout and confirmed the actual reload loader fails with a tensor shape mismatch, establishing that the new regression would fail before the existing production correction.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-41e2ae4a818a/raw/gfx950_loader_check.txt records the one-GPU BF16 loader check on AMD Instinct MI355X.

remaining_limitations: No Ascend NPU was available, so the original CANN/torch_npu execution path and scheduler subprocess behavior were not run.
The reported DeepSeekV3.2 model weights were unavailable; no full-model or HTTP update_weights_from_disk reproduction is claimed.
The gfx950 check validates FusedMoE tensor loading only and does not qualify NPU kernel execution, model semantics, or distributed behavior.
